html.name: New York
html.hero.eyebrow: Strong flour · 48 h cold ferment · BIG HORN
html.hero.lead: A hand-made New York-style pizza recipe for home: a firm dough with olive oil and a touch of sugar, 48 hours in the fridge and a gentler oven. Consolidated from classic recipes and not yet tested in the BIG HORN; the numbers will be revised after the first test bake.
html.panel.note: Defaults = version 0.1, consolidated from classic recipes and not yet tested. Your values are saved in this browser.
html.recipe.sub: Total dough quantities. Straight dough: every ingredient goes into the same mix.
html.steps.sub: Tick each step when done. Tags show the source: classic New York technique, or an adaptation for hand mixing and the BIG HORN.
html.oven.sub: Bench timer and diagnosis by result. New York pizza bakes slower: 5 to 7 minutes, turning every minute.
html.oven.note: Orange band: 1–1.5 min, time for the first turn. Green band: 5–7 min, the expected window.
html.rules.sub: A starting point with no bakes yet. After the first test, these rules become lessons.

rules: Use strong flour, 13% protein or more.
Cold water: the dough will spend 2 days in the fridge.
Knead properly: New York dough needs strong gluten.
Oil goes in once the dough has come together.
Little yeast: the fridge does the work.
Take the dough out 2 h before baking.
No rolling pin: stretch with hands and knuckles.
A gentler oven than for Neapolitan.
Finish with Parmesan, oregano and chili flakes.
The slice must fold without cracking.
Change one variable at a time.
glossary: Flour with 13–15% protein (like Caputo Manitoba Oro). It builds more gluten and gives New York pizza its chew.
Leaving the dough balls 1 to 3 days in the fridge. The yeast works slowly and the dough gains flavour and stretch.
Stretching a piece of dough into a thin membrane without tearing. A sign the gluten is ready.
The firm block mozzarella you shred. It melts without releasing water, unlike fresh mozzarella.
Folding the slice lengthwise to eat it on the go, the New York way.
Coarse durum wheat flour dusted on the peel. It acts like ball bearings so the pizza slides.

about.sub: Where this recipe comes from and what defines New York pizza.
site: This is the first version of New York pizza on NapoliProtocol. It consolidates classic home recipes for New York-style pizza and adapts the result to this site's process: hand-mixed dough, a fridge at about 7 °C and a BIG HORN electric oven.

The formula sits in the middle of what those references use: strong flour, 63% hydration, 2% salt, 2.5% olive oil, 1.5% sugar and little yeast, because this fridge is warmer than the 3–4 °C most American recipes assume.
There hasn't been a bake yet. After the first test, the numbers get recalibrated, the lessons go into the steps and the recipe becomes version 1.0, as happened with the Neapolitan.
pizza: New York pizza was born with immigrants from southern Italy. Lombardi's, opened by Gennaro Lombardi, is considered the city's first licensed pizzeria, in 1905, baking in a coal-fired oven.

With gas deck ovens after the Second World War, pizza became counter food: large pies of about 18 inches (45 cm) sold by the slice. The dough uses strong flour, a little oil and sometimes sugar, and bakes for several minutes at around 260–340 °C.

The result is thin, crisp underneath and pliable on top. It comes with seasoned tomato sauce and low-moisture mozzarella almost to the edge, and you eat it by folding the slice in half. At home the size is limited by the stone; the logic of the dough stays the same.

ev: Steps 01–04. About 2 h, including a 1 h rest at room temperature.
Step 06. Make the sauce and cheese meanwhile.
sched.past: Start is in the past. To bake at that time, the dough should already have been made. Push the bake back or shorten the fridge time.
sched.over36: More than 72 h in the fridge. The dough tends to turn sour and weak.

warn.hyd: Hydration differs from 63%. For version 0.1, start with the defaults.
warn.per: Dough balls of {per} g are outside the 280–320 g range for the BIG HORN stone. See the alternative or adjust the flour.
warn.bottom: A bottom element above 330 °C tends to burn the base before the cheese browns.

msg: Turn every ~1 min. Watch the rim and the cheese.
Done window. Check the base and the browned cheese.
Past 7 min. If it's still pale, it needs more heat.

diag: Base burns before the cheese browns
Cheese burns or gets very oily
Bake faster with a little more heat, or raise the oil to 3%.
Overbaked or stretched too thin. Pull it earlier or stretch a little less.
Less sauce, low-moisture mozzarella and a well-heated stone before launching.

li: Dry-mix {flour} g of flour, {yeast} g of yeast and {sugar} g of sugar.
Dissolve {salt} g of salt in {water} g of cold water (10–15 °C).
Pour the water into the flour and mix until no dry flour is left.
Cover and rest 20 min. The flour hydrates and the kneading gets shorter.
items.tip: Cold water holds the fermentation back: the dough still has 2 days in the fridge ahead.

li: Add {oil} g of olive oil a little at a time.
Work it in with pincers and folds until the dough absorbs it all and stops slipping.
Knead 8–10 min on the bench with no extra flour: push with the heel of your hand, fold and give a quarter turn.
Rest 10 min and knead 2–3 min more, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Windowpane test: stretch a piece into a thin membrane. If it tears right away, knead a little more.
items.tip: New York dough needs more gluten than Neapolitan. That's what makes the slice foldable and chewy.

li: Shape into a ball, place it in a lightly oiled bowl and cover.
Leave 1 h at room temperature. It should rise only a little.
Divide into {n} dough balls of {per} g (total dough {total} g).
Ball with surface tension and seal the base well.
Individual lightly oiled tubs, covered, in the fridge for about {panh} h.
items.tip: At {fridge} °C fermentation moves faster than at the 3–4 °C of American recipes, which is why the yeast is low. If your fridge is colder, go up to 0.3%.

li: Take them out of the fridge about {outh} h before baking, still in the covered tub.
Ready when: relaxed, slightly puffy, bubbles on the sides and soft to the touch.
items.tip: warn|Cold dough won't stretch: it shrinks and tears. Give it the full time out.

li: Briefly blend or pass through a food mill {cans} can(s) of peeled tomatoes: a smooth, thick, uncooked sauce.
Season with 4–5 g of salt per can and 1 teaspoon of dried oregano. Optional: a pinch of sugar and 1 grated garlic clove.
Coarsely shred {cheeseTotal} g of low-moisture mozzarella (the firm block kind).
Set aside grated Parmesan, oregano and chili flakes for finishing.
items.tip: Fresh mozzarella releases too much water for the longer New York bake.

li: Top element at {top} °C, bottom element at {bottom} °C.
If you have an infrared thermometer, measure the centre of the stone: the target is ~290–320 °C.
items.tip: warn|Starting values, not yet tested in this oven. Use the diagnosis below to calibrate.

li: Flour the dough ball well on both sides.
Press the centre with your fingertips, leaving about a 1 cm rim.
Lift the dough and stretch it over your knuckles, rotating, to ~30–32 cm.
The disc ends up thin and even, with an almost translucent centre.
items.tip: No rolling pin. If the dough springs back, rest it 5–10 min and continue.

li: Dust the peel with semolina and lay the disc on it.
Spread {sauce} g of sauce in a thin layer, up to ~1 cm from the edge.
Cover with {cheese} g of shredded mozzarella, almost to the edge.
Give it a short sideways shake: the whole pizza must slide.
Turn 90–180° every ~1 min for an even bake.
Done when: cheese melted with browned spots and a golden rim.
Lift the edge with the peel: the base should be firm and spotted, not pale.
items.tip: New York pizza bakes slower and cooler than Neapolitan: crisp underneath, pliable on top.

li: Rest 1–2 min on a wire rack so the base doesn't go soft.
Finish with Parmesan, oregano and chili flakes.
Cut into 6 to 8 slices. To eat, fold the slice in half.
